strengths: Principled optimization-theoretic framework deriving token weights from constrained optimization over gradient utilities, yielding closed-form Gibbs distribution solution
Efficient one-backward probing trick reduces token utility estimation from |y| backward passes to one backward + |y| forward passes, making the approach scalable for long sequences (~3000 tokens)
Well-motivated variance-controlled scaling mechanism with clear empirical validation (Figure 3) showing necessity for training stability

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 model sizes (Qwen3 4B/8B/32B, LLaMA3.1-8B), 2 domains (math, coding), in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks (6 total), with systematic ablations on dataset size and hyperparameters
Consistent improvements over competitive baselines (DFT, iw-SFT) across most settings, with particularly strong relative gains on smaller models (LLaMA +5.84 pts, Qwen3-4B +3.6 pts)
Downstream RL experiments and analysis of performance across task difficulty levels (GSM8K vs MATH500)
weaknesses: First-order Taylor approximation (Eq. 1) validity only established for small learning rates, but no analysis of approximation quality bounds or failure conditions provided; link between maximizing single-step loss descent and improved generalization is assumed rather than theoretically justified

Empirical improvements often marginal and statistically unvalidated: Qwen3-8B Math (35.74→35.80), Code (35.07→35.26), AIME results single-digit without error bars or significance tests; no confidence intervals or multi-run averaging reported

Evaluation restricted to DeepSeek-R1 generated CoTs only; authors acknowledge not exploring 'more diverse datasets or long CoT data produced by other state-of-the-art reasoning models'; GSM8K results show degradation across all methods, suggesting limited generalization to varying task difficulty

Despite robustness claims, method introduces two new hyperparameters (ε, τ) requiring per-model tuning via grid search; Figure 2(b) shows non-negligible performance variations; no principled hyperparameter selection method provided

Limited baseline comparisons: only DFT and iw-SFT evaluated; other approaches (entropy filtering, confidence thresholds, influence-based weighting) mentioned but not compared; no ablation isolating Gibbs distribution impact from variance control

No analysis of learned weight distributions or which token types receive higher weights; missing comparison to simple baselines like entropy-based weighting; no error analysis or failure case investigation
Acknowledged failure mode (reweighting amplifying spurious answer-leaking patterns) not addressed empirically; suggested fixes (dropout masking, answer prefix control) mentioned but not implemented

Mixed RL downstream results (Table 2): VCORE sometimes starts with lower baseline accuracy; limited to 200 RL steps potentially insufficient for strong conclusions; 'higher upper bound' claim only weakly supported
Inconsistent experimental setup: 3.2k training examples for Qwen3 vs 32k for LLaMA, different LoRA ranks (8 vs 64), single seed (no variance estimates), arbitrary Random baseline (80% dropout)
No code availability mentioned; reproducibility limited by hardware specificity (RTX 6000 Blackwell) and LLaMA-Factory dependency; hyperparameter selection procedure incompletely described

strengths: Principled optimization-theoretic framework deriving token weights from constrained optimization with closed-form Gibbs solution (Theorem 1)
Practical one-backward probing trick efficiently estimating token utilities in O(1) backward passes instead of O(|y|), enabling scalability
Variance control mechanism (α = √(V_u/V_q)) is essential and empirically validated to stabilize training under sharp reweighting (Figure 3)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 model sizes, 2 domains, in/out-of-domain benchmarks, with detailed ablations and component analysis
Consistent improvements especially on lower-capacity models (Qwen-4B gains of +3.6% on average across benchmarks)
Demonstrated effectiveness as RL initialization providing better downstream reasoning performance (Table 4)
Well-documented with extensive appendices, implementation details, and theoretical proofs supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: core contribution is standard exponential tilting with KL constraints; Gibbs solution is textbook result rather than novel optimization methodology
Modest empirical improvements in key scenarios: 2% average gain over SFT (31.03 vs 28.97), <1% on Qwen-32B, inconsistent across model scales making practical benefit unclear
First-order approximation only; extension to AdamW is 'local extension' not exact derivation, weakening theoretical grounding for actual implementation; impact of O(η²) terms not analyzed

Severely limited dataset diversity: all CoT from single source (DeepSeek-R1) in only two domains (math/coding); paper acknowledges 'not yet explored more diverse datasets,' limiting generalization claims
Unresolved acknowledged failure mode: method can 'overemphasize spurious patterns leaking answer information' but proposed mitigations (dropout, answer masking) never tested or implemented
Computational overhead substantially understated: Table 12 shows 44-215% overhead depending on setup; claim that |B'|≪|B| makes overhead 'negligible' contradicts empirical data
Hyperparameter tuning required despite robustness claims: Table 7 shows different τ,ε across models; limited guidance without grid search; only 4 configurations tested
Degradation on simpler tasks unexplained: VCORE hurts GSM8K (-0.99%) but helps MATH500 (+2.4%), suggesting long CoT harmful for simple reasoning; only superficial analysis provided
No statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or error bars despite modest improvements and multiple comparisons; some gains may be noise
Inconsistent results across models and domains: Qwen-8B improvements much smaller than Qwen-4B; results vary unpredictably making it difficult to predict when VCORE helps
